title: Disable dormant users
use_case: When Sophos ITDR flags a user as dormant, disable the account in Entra ID if it's cloud-only. It needs only the Microsoft Graph API connection. For on-premises and synced accounts, use Disable dormant users in Active Directory.
trigger: Platform Events, source Identity Findings, event Created only. Set When does this playbook run? to Only When, with inputs.identityFindings.new.check.category.toLower() == 'dormant_resource' && inputs.identityFindings.new.primaryReference.derivedType == 'USER'
connections: Taegis.MicrosoftGraphAPI 2.12.2, the Microsoft Graph API connector Sophos manages, to look users up and disable cloud-only accounts
requires: Sophos ITDR with Microsoft Entra ID connected, and Sophos Fusion playbooks under Security Operations > Automations
mdr_note: Sophos MDR doesn't run or watch this playbook, and it doesn't change what Sophos MDR does.
rollback: Enable User: enable the account again in Entra ID, and add it to Excluded users so a later finding doesn't disable it again.
author: Aaronjacobs000
summary: This playbook disables a cloud-only user in Entra ID when Sophos ITDR flags the user as dormant, and skips users synced from Active Directory. A new dormant identity finding starts it, and it calls only the Microsoft Graph API connector Sophos manages, with dry run on and only the domains you list in scope. It needs Sophos ITDR.
notes:
Setup:
- It needs only the Microsoft Graph API connection. For accounts in on-premises Active Directory, synced or not, add Disable dormant users in Active Directory, which needs only the LDAP connection. With both directories, use both.
- Version 1.0.0 also disabled on-premises and synced accounts, and needed both connections. Version 2.0.0 is a major version, so a playbook configured from 1.0.0 doesn't move to it on its own.
- ITDR's dormant threshold is fixed: 90 days without a sign-in for Dormant Accounts. Posture Check Preferences only turns checks on or off.
- For a 30-day rule, or without Sophos ITDR, use the Disable inactive users playbook in this library.
- The trigger is Created only, so findings that exist before you turn it on don't start a run. Find those with the Directory's Is Dormant filter.
- There's no approval step. Dry run, Domains and Excluded users are the controls.

How it works:
- It looks the user up in Entra ID by the finding's object ID, or by user principal name, and disables a cloud-only account there.
- It skips a user synced from Active Directory. Active Directory is the source of authority under Entra Connect Sync, so a disable in Entra ID alone can be undone at the next sync.
- It never disables a user ITDR flags as an admin.
- Identity findings take no comments, so the result is the execution's outcome under Playbooks > Executions.

Testing:
- Not run in a tenant yet.
- On 2026-11-03 this version's dsl passed playbookValidateDSLV2 with no errors or warnings in a Sophos Fusion test tenant. It wasn't imported. On 2026-11-02 a renamed copy of version 1.0.0 imported and exported again unchanged.
- Every step ran in Sophos Fusion's CEL engine, through its evaluateExpr API, against 23 made-up findings and connector replies: cloud-only, synced, not in Entra ID, excluded, admin, out of scope, already disabled, refused and findings it doesn't act on.
- The check titles and the DORMANT_RESOURCE category come from a test tenant's ITDR checks. It had no identity provider connected, so it had no real dormant finding.

Known gaps:
- A real dormant finding is untested. The playbook reads it through the documented finding macros, which return an empty list for a field the event lacks. A finding with no user principal name or object ID ends in FAIL.
- Saving it with only the Microsoft Graph API connection is untested. Sophos Fusion asks for a connection to each connector a template lists, and this one lists only that one.
- There's no daily cap. A newly connected directory can create many dormant findings at once, and each run disables one user.
